pass_a_gloss: And how is the measure of confession filled, or not filled but left lacking, so we might contemplate. If through the whole time of the examination and of the trial we should not give place to the slanderer in our hearts, he wanting to stain us with wicked reasonings of denial or of two-souledness or of some persuasiveness calling out toward the things hostile to the witness-death and to the completeness, and toward this if we should not even with a word foreign to the confession stain ourselves, and if we should carry all the reproach from the opposed ones and jeering and laughter and evil-speaking and pity, which they seem to pity us with, supposing us to be led astray and dull and calling us tripped up, and further if we should not be dragged about, being pulled around, also by the fond affection about the children or their mother or some of those reckoned to be dearest in the life, toward the possession or toward this living, but having turned away from all these we should become whole of God and of the life with him and beside him, as going to share with his only-born one and with his sharers, then we might say that we filled the measure of the confession; but if even in one something we should lack, we did not fill but stained the measure of the confession and mixed into it something foreign. For which reason we will need what those need who built upon the foundation woods or grass or stalk.
pass_b_english: How the measure of confession is filled, or is not filled but falls short, we might consider in this way. Suppose that throughout the whole time of examination and temptation we give no place to the devil in our hearts (Ephesians 4:27), when he wishes to defile us with evil thoughts of denial, or of a divided soul, or of some plausible argument that calls us towards what is hostile to martyrdom and to perfection. Suppose, besides, that we do not stain ourselves with even a word foreign to confession, and that we bear all the reproach from our opponents, their mockery and laughter and slander, and the pity with which they think they pity us, when they suppose us to be deluded and foolish and call us misguided. Suppose, further, that we are not dragged about and distracted, by affection for our children or their mother or any of those thought dearest in this life, towards possessions or towards this life, but turn away from all these and become wholly God's, and wholly given to the life with him and beside him, as those who are to share with his Only-begotten and with those who share in him. Then we could say that we have filled up the measure of confession.

But if we fall short even in a single thing, we have not filled up the measure of confession but have defiled it, and mixed into it something foreign to it. So we shall need what those need who have built upon the foundation wood or hay or straw (1 Corinthians 3:12).
